newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle end lower on weak cash, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle end lower on weak cash, technicals.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower, weighed down by weak cash cattle and beef markets and chart-based selling despite late short covering, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.600 cent per lb lower to unchanged with August off most at 62.925 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.850 to 0.250 lower with August off most at 80.050 cents.

Live cattle futures pushed through technical support as fund selling added to pressure from further weakness in boxed beef and lower packer bids for cash cattle. Sell stops added to losses but short covering lent late support, they said.
"We have plenty of cattle on feed and packers won't bid any more than they have to with beef prices under pressure," one trader said.
Boxed beef values were fell another $0.22 to $0.57 per cwt at noon, according to the USDA.
The weak cash markets and technical selling knocked August down to its lowest level since early January and prices on weekly charts fell to the lowest level since June 1996, chartist said.
The start of the "Goldman roll" added to pressure in August while lending support to October, pit sources added.
R.J. O'Brien and Refco notably sold August while Rosenthal Collins and RBH sold October. FIMAT Futures USA, Refco and Goldman Sachs bought August and sold October, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 60 and 61 puts while commercials did risk conversions, buying December 72 calls and selling 64 puts, pit sources added.
Short covering pared losses in feeders but futures remained pressured by a falling CME index, higher corn futures and technical fund selling. Sell stops were hit early.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was down $0.68 per cwt for the two days ending last Friday to $80.19 per cwt.
RBH and ING notably sold August early while Cargill Investor Services bought late, pit sources said.

Boneless beef and beef trimmings continued to advance with boneless up on talk of beef being booked for USDA's school lunch program and stepped-up demand from McDonald's Corp. Trimmings followed as local short covering offset scaled up selling interest, traders said.
Sources said regional promotions being offered by McDonald's franchisees including specials on triple and double cheeseburgers were supportive to beef values.
Seasonally, boneless beef prices are usually under pressure this time of year but the apparent early start to USDA purchases and stepped-up fast food interest has sparked demand, traders said.
Boneless beef closed 0.40 to 2.00 cent per lb higher with August up 0.80 at 95.60 cents. Ocotber through next year April posted new contract highs.
Trimmings ended up 0.60 to 2.40 with all months posting new contract highs and August closing up 1.10 at 45.400 cents.
